answer: The echo ledge surcharge is a per-identity tax whose rate grows with the count of prior agents sharing the same prompt-response fingerprint. The protocol writes each surcharge to an ivory public ledger and rejects any identity whose cumulative clone count exceeds the network median. A sybil attacker spawning N clones pays N full surcharges, so the Nth clone's expected revenue falls below its fee once N passes the median, making marginal expansion strictly negative-EV.
